subject: Dedicated Reservation Proposal & Ramp Options for QuantumPay
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <amorgan@quantumpay.io>

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@quantumpay.io>
Date: 2026-08-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: preliminary capacity questions

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for the demo last week. We ran internal cost modeling and want to understand options for a reserved GPU plan that fits our projected growth. Two quick questions: 1) what minimum cluster size do you recommend for predictable 95th-percentile latency under heavy load, and 2) how do ramp schedules map to pricing/credits?

We expect peak concurrency of ~850 concurrent users across several chat and batch embedding workloads by Q4, with steady-state token rate estimates attached here (see: gpu_capacity_modeling.xlsx).

Would like to align on a reservation option we can include in our procurement RFP.

Thanks,
Alex
VP Product, QuantumPay

Attachments: gpu_capacity_modeling.xlsx (spreadsheet, 74 KB)
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <amorgan@quantumpay.io>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-11T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: preliminary capacity questions

Alex —

Appreciate the details and the attachment. High level answer up front: for an 850 concurrent-user peak with mixed chat (low-latency) and batch embedding traffic, we typically recommend a reserved pool in the 64–96 GPU range (A100/H100 equivalence) with a minimum active slice of ~32 GPUs to preserve latency SLAs during normal hours and burst capacity for predictable peaks.

I'll outline three reservation options below (quick summary) and attach a formal proposal PDF. Dev, can you confirm the mapping from their spreadsheet to the proposal assumptions?

Summary (options):
- Option A — Conservative: 32 GPU reserved minimum, can burst to 64. Lower monthly commit, higher burst overage rates. Good if you want small upfront spend.
- Option B — Balanced (recommended): 48 GPUs reserved baseline, soft cap to 96 with scheduled ramp; 12-month commit with gradual phase-up. Best balance of cost and consistent latency.
- Option C — Aggressive: 96 GPUs reserved, includes priority capacity and lower per-GPU-hour rate; recommended for enterprise SLA and aggressive growth.

Ramp scheduling: we offer a staged ramp tied to milestone payments — e.g., Month 0–2: 50% of baseline, Month 3–5: 75%, Month 6+: 100% — or a faster 3-month ramp if procurement requires. Pricing scales with committed baseline; bursts above committed are billed at an overage rate or consumed from a shared burst pool depending on the contract.

I'll drop a formal proposal to the folder (QuantumPay_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf). Laura, would finance like a sketch of the commitment P&L and refund/cancel rules for the RFP?

Cheers,
Rishi
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: QuantumPay_Dedicated_Proposal_v1.pdf (proposal, 210 KB)
From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-12T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: preliminary capacity questions

Alex / Rishi —

I mapped the spreadsheet numbers to expected GPU utilization curves and validated the 48 baseline recommendation for mixed chat + batch. Key assumptions: 1) model footprint equivalent to 70B dense model quantized to 4-bit; 2) average sequence length 350 tokens for chat; 3) batch embedding windows processed in 5–10s jobs. Under these assumptions:

- 48 GPUs baseline -> target p95 latency at peak: 300–450ms for chat (with continuous batching).
- 32 GPUs baseline -> p95 latency degrades to ~600ms during sustained peaks; acceptable for non-real-time flows.
- 96 GPUs baseline -> p95 latency <250ms and provides headroom for additional product features.

Operational notes: we recommend a canary pool (8 GPUs) for new model versions and an autoscale buffer of 10–15% to avoid cold-start stalls. Cache and prefix reuse will reduce effective token cost; we included conservative cache-hit assumptions in the attached modeling.

Happy to walk through the numbers with your infra/engineering team — happy to set a call.

— Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Alex —

Thanks for the early context. From CS/ops perspective, a staged ramp is easier to operate against than a single large commit. Proposal items to include in the RFP:

- Explicit ramp schedule with dates and GPU counts per month (we usually provide a 3- or 6-month ramp template).
- Minimum guaranteed capacity (helps our placement logic) and a documented burst policy (how many GPUs can be borrowed and at what cost).
- Runbook for failover (fallback to lower-spec quantized variants) and rollback windows.
- Clear metrics to be reported monthly (p95 latency, 99th percentile error rate, token counts).

Also flag: SOC2 evidence request likely needed by procurement. I'm attaching a short SOC2 summary to the Drive folder.

Best,
Marissa
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-18T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation commercial questions

Hi Procurement —

Thanks for the clear questions. Commercial answers below (high level):

1) Minimum committed term: Options A/B/C are available for 3-, 6-, or 12-month commits. We recommend 12 months for deepest discounts; 3-month options carry a small premium but provide flexibility.

2) Unused committed GPU-hours: We provide an offset credit pool for unused committed hours on a quarterly basis. For 12-month contracts, up to 20% of unused committed hours in a quarter can be rolled forward once; for 3–6 month contracts, unused hours are credited at 70% value and expire at quarter end. We also offer a capacity rebalancing window at Month 3 to adjust baseline counts without penalty (one-time).

3) Billing cadence: Monthly billing with month-ahead invoicing is standard; quarterly invoicing is available for enterprise customers.

4) Trial/credit window: We can provide up to 30 days of on-platform credits (applies to burst usage) with a one-time grace period on initial overage charges while onboarding is completed.

Next steps: Rishi will confirm the final option and ramp schedule for the SOW. Grace/Marissa — please prepare the operational SLA appendix and the ramp template doc for the RFP folder.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference
